protocol: Held video benchmarks (GenVideo-Val, VideoPhy, VidProM, EvalCrafter): bench_eval_video --limit L with L = ceil(250 / n_generators), the first L sorted reals and the first L sorted fakes of every generator (video_layout.discover order); EvalCrafter has no reals and is paired with the first L GenVideo-Val MSR-VTT reals (the convention of the merged video matrix: --reals GenVideo/test/Crafter/0_real). GenBuster-Bench / GenBuster-Bench++ (the paper's GB / GB++): the first ceil(fraction * n) sorted clips of every folder (each generator's fakes and the one real pool), keeping the benchmark's real : fake composition. subsets/<bench>.json lists every file with its sha1. The agent and every comparator score byte-identical files.
rank_note: rank_<metric> = 1 + the number of comparators strictly better (the agent among the comparators plus itself); acc_strict is ranked against the comparators' acc (they have no tool errors); best and median are over the comparators only
acc_note: acc: bench_eval_video's balanced accuracy (mean of real and fake accuracy per generator, then the mean over generators); for the agent from its verdict (unparsed = wrong for both classes), official = final tool_error / oom videos excluded with their counts reported, strict = counted wrong. pooled: one row per distinct video (the paper's metric)

paper_note: WeVisForensics arXiv 2611.21373: Table 4 / Table 12 report accuracy (Acc.), fake recall (R) and F1 with the generated videos as the positive class, one row per clip (official scripts/evaluate.py: invalid answers count wrong, tool_error rows are excluded). The paper's run is the official vLLM engine (multi-GPU, its own kernels); ours is the official transformers backend (demo/wvf_local.py) under SynthScope's runner, greedy, audio off (has_audio=False for every clip; GenBuster clips are silent), on a documented subsample. implied_real_acc is derived from Acc. and R and the benchmark's composition (an inference, not printed). The paper's NSG-VD and ReStraV rows are those detectors RETRAINED by the authors on their training data, not the public checkpoints scored here. IN-DOMAIN: GenBuster-Bench is the paper's in-domain benchmark and GenBuster-200K is in WeVisForensics' training data (paper Sec. 3, training sources), so GB and GB++ are NOT held out for wevis, while every comparator here was trained elsewhere: wevis ranking first on them is not a held-out result. The held-out comparison is the four held subsets (subset_means.held4).
